answer: Fixed-pool dilution bond starves mass fakes: a 40,000-credit pool per epoch is split among lantern claims. Each identity posts 70 credits and lights its lantern. Auditors wander and re-check the board; a dark lantern burns its bond, and a rented one fails when its lender cannot relight it. Fees climb by a delta of 6 per filing, so the k-th costs 46+6(k-1): 1,000 fakes pay 3,043,000 for a 40,000 pool; honest agents pay 46 once and keep the bond.
